newsitem.title: USA: Hilton seeks fast resolution to ITT offer.
newsitem.headline: Hilton seeks fast resolution to ITT offer.

text.p: Hilton Hotels Corp Chief Executive Officer Stephen Bollenbach on Monday said he wants to speed the process of resolving its proposed $6.5 billion takeover of ITT Corp.

"While we remain prepared to take the question directly to your shareholders, a faster resolution of this important matter is in everyone's interest," Bollenbach wrote in a letter to ITT Chairman Rand Araskog.
Earlier in the day, Hilton filed a proxy solicitation to ITT Corp shareholders seeking votes for a Hilton-nominated slate of directors who would replace ITT's board.

But a shareholder vote on the matter would have to wait until ITT's next annual meeting. Last year, ITT held the meeting on May 14, but it has yet to schedule one for this year. By law in Nevada, where ITT is incorporated, it does not have to hold the annual meeting until mid-November.
"Waiting for your regularly scheduled May annual meeting will only result in a lost opportunity for our companies and shareholders," Bollenbach wrote.

He noted Marriott International Inc's $1.billion offer for Renaissance Hotel Group last week "serves as a reminder that our competitors will not stand still awaiting the completion of a combination of Hilton and ITT."
Bollenbach also urged caution in selling assets, which ITT has said it would do as part of a plan to refocus operations on core businesses in hotels and gambling.

"A true focus on your core businesses involves more than simply selling non-strategic assets," he wrote. "We are confident that your shareholders will realize more value from a combination with Hilton than they would from any quick-fix financial engineering transactions."
